verifier: adversarial verification pass (default stance REFUTE); every cited file:line reopened in the pinned tree, every absence claim re-grepped independently, and the P1 reproductions re-run zero-network against the tree.

findings.title: Registry currency lookup is first-match-wins over a suffix test, so an apex row shadows its own country subdomains (om.swissarabian.com -> USD, not OMR)
findings.claim: `_registry_currency_for_host` returns the FIRST SOURCE_REGISTRY row whose domain is a suffix of the host, so `om.swissarabian.com` resolves to the `swissarabian.com` row and yields currency 'USD' instead of the OMR its own registry row declares.
findings.evidence: app/services/shopify_pdp_service.py:711-717 iterates `for source in SOURCE_REGISTRY:` and returns on the first `key == domain or key.endswith('.' + domain)` hit. data/bh_gcc_sources.json carries three separate live rows: swissarabian.com (currency USD, country BH, file index 128), ksa.swissarabian.com (SAR, index 133) and om.swissarabian.com (OMR, index 163). `_load_catalog_rows` (app/services/source_router.py:504-521) appends rows in FILE order, so the apex is always reached first. Executed against this tree with ENABLE_BH_GCC_CATALOG_SOURCES=true: `_registry_currency_for_host('om.swissarabian.com') = 'USD'`, `_registry_currency_for_host('ksa.swissarabian.com') = 'USD'`, while the correctly-ordered sibling pair `sa.ghawali.com` -> 'SAR' / `ghawali.com` -> 'AED' proves the lookup is order-dependent, not domain-correct.
findings.failure_scenario: ENABLE_UCP_JSON_PRICE is on (it is in the M10 activation family, runbook step 1) and a PDP on om.swissarabian.com is selected. `fetch_ucp_json_product` (shopify_pdp_service.py:884-885) gates only on `is_shopify_pdp_path(pdp_url)` — a URL-SHAPE check, not the registry `is_shopify` flag — then passes `_registry_currency_for_host(host)` as `registry_currency`. When the /products/*.json body omits `price_currency`, an Omani price of 25.000 OMR is stamped USD and converted to BHD at the USD rate: ~0.0094 vs ~0.0975 BHD per minor unit, i.e. the shelf price is understated by ~2.6x and the wrong product can win the comparison on price.
findings.fix_sketch: Resolve by LONGEST matching registry domain, not first-in-list: collect all suffix matches and return the one with the longest `domain` (exact match wins outright). Same change is needed in every `for s in SOURCE_REGISTRY` suffix scan (source_router.py:557, 593, 897, 920, 1122; price_service.py:13620; shopify_pdp_service.py:711; search_descriptor_service.py:216). A cheap guard test: assert `_registry_currency_for_host(row['domain']) == row['currency']` for every live row in data/bh_gcc_sources.json — it fails today on exactly the two swissarabian children.
findings.verify_evidence: MECHANISM REPRODUCED. app/services/shopify_pdp_service.py:711-717 is verbatim `for source in SOURCE_REGISTRY:` ... `if key == domain or key.endswith("." + domain): ... return code` — first suffix hit wins. Ran against this tree with ENABLE_BH_GCC_CATALOG_SOURCES=true: _registry_currency_for_host('om.swissarabian.com')='USD', ('ksa.swissarabian.com')='USD', ('sa.ghawali.com')='SAR', ('ghawali.com')='AED'. I wrote the reviewer's own proposed guard test (assert lookup(row.domain)==row.currency for all 319 registry rows) and it fails on EXACTLY 2 rows: ksa.swissarabian.com (want SAR got USD) and om.swissarabian.com (want OMR got USD). Registry order confirmed apex-first (idx swissarabian.com=... < ksa=177 < om=207). Enumerated ALL parent/child pairs in the registry independently: 5 exist (bahrain.sharafdg/sharafdg, bahrain.ounass/ounass, ksa.swissarabian/swissarabian, sa.ghawali/ghawali, om.swissarabian/swissarabian); only the 2 swissarabian children are shadowed. FAILURE SCENARIO WEAKENED, hence the downgrade: the finding's scenario requires the /products/{handle}.json body to OMIT price_currency, but the same module's measured header (shopify_pdp_service.py:589-596) records 'on all 32 [HTTP 200 handles across the 6 UCP hosts] the variant carries BOTH a major-unit decimal price and a self-declared price_currency — 32/32 equal to the registry currency', and om.swissarabian.com is one of those 6 hosts (pinned by name at price_service.py:13617-13619). parse_ucp_products_json:775-777 uses the registry value only as `declared or fallback`. Add that ENABLE_UCP_JSON_PRICE is default OFF (shopify_pdp_service.py:647) and _registry_currency_for_host has exactly one caller (line 885) and the wrong-currency stamp is a second-order fallback, not a live path. Also correcting the fix_sketch: price_service.py:13620 is _curl_timeout_for_url, a tier=='bahrain' filter loop, not a first-match currency scan — it does not need the same change. Real defect, wrong blast radius.

findings.title: descriptor_for_host has the same apex-shadowing bug: the Oman and KSA Swiss Arabian stores resolve to the global (USD) storefront's search endpoint
findings.claim: `descriptor_for_host` returns the first SOURCE_REGISTRY row whose domain is a suffix of the host, so the per-host search descriptor seeded for `om.swissarabian.com` / `ksa.swissarabian.com` is never used — both hosts get `swissarabian.com`'s template.
findings.evidence: app/services/search_descriptor_service.py:216-221 (`for source in SOURCE_REGISTRY: ... if domain == registry_domain or domain.endswith('.' + registry_domain): return desc`). data/search_descriptors.json seeds distinct usable templates for all three hosts (`https://om.swissarabian.com/search/suggest.json?q={q}...`, `https://ksa.swissarabian.com/...`, `https://swissarabian.com/...`) and all three are folded onto their registry rows in data/bh_gcc_sources.json. Executed with ENABLE_SEARCH_DESCRIPTOR=true + ENABLE_BH_GCC_CATALOG_SOURCES=true: `resolve_search_url('om.swissarabian.com','sauvage')` -> `https://swissarabian.com/search/suggest.json?q=sauvage&...` and the same for the ksa host.
findings.failure_scenario: CLAUDE.md:334 records that the descriptor store is SEEDED and that 'runbook step (6) is now a pure flag-flip'. On that flip, discovery for the Oman and Saudi Swiss Arabian storefronts silently queries the USD global store instead — the search returns global-catalogue handles, the resulting PDP URL is on the wrong storefront, and any price harvested from it carries the wrong currency for the requested region. 2 of the 47 usable templates (4%) are dead on arrival, and the failure is invisible: a valid URL comes back, just for the wrong store.
findings.fix_sketch: Longest-domain-wins, shared with data-01 (a single `_registry_row_for_host(host)` helper that all suffix scans call). Add a test asserting `descriptor_for_host(h).url_template.startswith('https://' + h)` for every host in data/search_descriptors.json that carries a `{q}` template.
findings.verify_evidence: REPRODUCED, and the code violates its own documented contract. app/services/search_descriptor_service.py:216-221 is the same first-match suffix scan (it does skip rows with no descriptor: `if desc is None: continue`, which I checked). Ran with ENABLE_SEARCH_DESCRIPTOR=true + ENABLE_BH_GCC_CATALOG_SOURCES=true: descriptor_for_host('om.swissarabian.com') and ('ksa.swissarabian.com') both return `https://swissarabian.com/search/suggest.json?q={q}&...`, i.e. NOT the per-host template the store seeds for them. I swept all 95 store hosts: exactly 2 resolve to a different template than the one persisted for them — the two swissarabian children. Store counts independently reproduced: 95 hosts, 47 with a {q} template, so 2/47 = 4% of usable templates are unreachable. DECISIVE: the function's own docstring at :195-199 states the intended contract — 'bh.afnan.com resolves under its OWN row; a regional subdomain of a registry apex resolves to the apex' — which is precisely what the implementation fails to do for a subdomain that HAS its own row. Post-flip (runbook step 6 is 'a pure flag-flip', CLAUDE.md:334) discovery for the Oman and Saudi storefronts silently queries the USD global store; the consumer price_service._descriptor_search_url:9089-9114 feeds it straight into build_retailer_url. Not a documented known item: grepped CLAUDE.md + docs/ for any record of apex/suffix shadowing — none.

findings.title: Migration 025's stated reason for keeping the users row is false, and the two user-scoped tables added after it (028, 029) are never cleaned by delete_user_cascade
findings.claim: `delete_user_cascade()` deliberately UPDATEs rather than DELETEs `public.users` 'so admin_audit_log foreign keys resolve' — but `admin_audit_log.user_id` has no foreign key at all, and because the parent row survives, the `ON DELETE CASCADE` that migrations 028 and 029 rely on can never fire.
findings.evidence: migrations/025_delete_user_cascade_completeness.sql:57 ('We keep the row so admin_audit_log foreign keys resolve') and :15-17 ('admin_audit_log: RETAIN'). migrations/011_security_completion_freemium.sql:37 declares `user_id UUID,` inside CREATE TABLE admin_audit_log — a bare column, no REFERENCES clause, no FK anywhere in migrations/*.sql. migrations/028_pain_workflow_events.sql:35 and migrations/029_user_preference_history.sql:45 both declare `user_id uuid NOT NULL REFERENCES public.users(id) ON DELETE CASCADE`, and 029's header (lines 20-24) asserts 'the migration 025 cascade extension covers this implicitly ... explicit CASCADE makes the FK-level guarantee match the function-level promise' — 025's function body (lines 34-69) never touches either table. By contrast migration 030's `verdict_critiques` FKs to `comparisons(id)`, which 025 DOES delete, so that one genuinely cascades — the asymmetry is the proof.
findings.failure_scenario: A user taps Delete Account. `auth_service.delete_user_account` (app/services/auth_service.py:499-506) calls `delete_user_cascade` then `admin.auth.admin.delete_user`. The function clears comparisons/feedback/usage/referrals and blanks the users row, but leaves every `pain_workflow_events` row (behavioural signal payloads) and every `user_preference_history` row (JSONB snapshots of the user's stated preferences, migration 029) keyed to that user id. Whether they eventually vanish depends on `public.users.id` FK-ing `auth.users(id) ON DELETE CASCADE` — DDL this repo does not contain, so it cannot be verified from the tree and is not asserted by any test. In the branch where it does cascade, 025's retention rationale is not just wrong but self-defeating (the row it 'keeps' is deleted a moment later); in the branch where it does not, the app retains deleted-user behavioural data indefinitely against its own App-Store delete-cascade claim.
findings.fix_sketch: (1) Run `SELECT confrelid::regclass, confdeltype FROM pg_constraint WHERE conrelid='public.users'::regclass` once and write the answer into CLAUDE.md's Migrations section — this is a one-query fact the repo has been guessing at for three migrations. (2) Either add explicit `DELETE FROM pain_workflow_events / user_preference_history WHERE user_id = target_user_id` to a migration 036 that re-CREATE-OR-REPLACEs the function, or delete the false admin_audit_log rationale and let the users row be dropped. (3) Correct 029's header comment either way.
findings.verify_evidence: SUB-CLAIMS VERIFIED, CONSEQUENCE OVERSTATED. Verified byte-for-byte: migrations/025:57 is '-- We keep the row so admin_audit_log foreign keys resolve, but every'; migrations/011:37 is '    user_id UUID,' (bare column). Independent absence check — `grep -rn 'REFERENCES public.users|REFERENCES users' migrations/*.sql` returns 9 hits (011:10, 014:20/27/39/40/49/63, 028:35, 029:45) and admin_audit_log is in NONE of them, so the retention rationale in 025 is factually false. 028:35 and 029:45 are both 'user_id uuid NOT NULL REFERENCES public.users(id) ON DELETE CASCADE' and 025's body (lines 34-69) touches neither table; 030:42 FKs to comparisons(id), which 025 does delete. BUT the finding's headline harm ('the app retains deleted-user behavioural data indefinitely') rests on 'DDL this repo does not contain' — it DOES contain it: docs/CONTEXT_DATABASE_API.md:83-84 records `CREATE TABLE public.users (id UUID PRIMARY KEY REFERENCES auth.users(id) ON DELETE CASCADE, ...)`, and auth_service.py:498-506 calls delete_user_data_cascade (database_service.py:149-157 -> rpc 'delete_user_cascade') and THEN admin.auth.admin.delete_user(user_id), so on the documented schema the users row is deleted a moment later and 028/029 cascade correctly. What survives is a real but doc-level defect: a false FK rationale in 025, a false 'migration 025 cascade extension covers this' claim in 029's header (lines 20-24), and a users-row retention that is self-defeating. Also partially KNOWN: docs/CONTEXT_DECISIONS_BUGS.md:18 already records the delete_user_cascade completeness gap and the unverified public.users->auth.users cascade (the 028/029 half is new, so known_item is set to true with the status claim intact, not wrong).

findings.title: CLAUDE.md's migration ledger stops at 032 and never mentions ENABLE_PRICE_TITLE_PERSIST — flipping it before 033/034 silently kills the entire L2 price-cache write, not just the new columns
findings.claim: The only place the repo records applied-migration state says 'Applied 010–032' and stops; 033 and 034 have no recorded status anywhere, and `ENABLE_PRICE_TITLE_PERSIST` — the flag whose precondition they are — does not appear in CLAUDE.md at all (grep count 0).
findings.evidence: CLAUDE.md:83 'Applied 010–032 (all via MCP since 013; 027–032 = Bundle B B.1 ...)'. CLAUDE.md:334 records 035 as unapplied; nothing records 033/034. `grep -c ENABLE_PRICE_TITLE_PERSIST CLAUDE.md` = 0, while the flag is live at app/services/product_data_service.py:43. app/services/product_data_service.py:195-204: when the flag is on, `row['title']` (and conditionally `row['in_stock']`) are added to the SAME dict that is passed to `client.table('product_prices').insert(row).execute()` at :204, inside one try whose except at :205-206 is a `logger.warning`.
findings.failure_scenario: An operator reads CLAUDE.md, finds no mention of 033/034 or the flag, and sets ENABLE_PRICE_TITLE_PERSIST=true on Railway before applying the migrations (the reverse of the order buried in the .sql headers). PostgREST rejects the insert with 'column product_prices.title does not exist' — the WHOLE row, so EVERY L2 price write stops, not just the title. The exception is swallowed into a warning at product_data_service.py:206, so the only symptom is that the L2 price cache stops filling: cold-compare rate climbs, Serper/Firecrawl spend climbs, and nothing turns red. The paired read at :118-124 degrades every L2 hit to a miss for the same reason.
findings.fix_sketch: Extend CLAUDE.md:83 to an explicit per-migration ledger through 035 with an APPLIED/UNAPPLIED stamp each, and add `ENABLE_PRICE_TITLE_PERSIST` to the Feature Flags paragraph with its migration precondition spelled out. Better: make the flag self-guarding — probe `information_schema.columns` once per process and log `[L2] title-persist requested but column absent — flag ignored` instead of taking the whole insert down.
findings.verify_evidence: ALL ABSENCE CLAIMS RE-CHECKED MYSELF. `grep -c` over CLAUDE.md: ENABLE_PRICE_TITLE_PERSIST = 0, '033' = 0, '034' = 0, '035' = 2 (both at line 334, and that line does stamp 035 '**unapplied**'). CLAUDE.md:83 reads 'Applied 010-032 ... Files in migrations/*.sql; rollbacks in migrations/rollback/*.sql' and stops. The code half is exact: product_data_service.py:43 reads the flag; :195-203 adds row['title'] (+ conditional row['in_stock']) to the SAME dict inserted at :204 `client.table('product_prices').insert(row).execute()`, inside one try whose handler at :205-206 is `logger.warning(f"Failed to save price for ...")` — so a missing column takes the WHOLE row write down silently; the read leg at :118-124 appends ', title' then ', brand, in_stock' to the select list under the same flag. Independently confirmed no self-guard exists: `grep -rn information_schema app/ scripts/` returns nothing, and the flag has no probe at any of its 7 call sites. Mitigation noted (does not change severity): the ordering hazard IS spelled out in the code docstring at :35-42 and in the 033/034 headers — it is only CLAUDE.md, the doc an operator actually reads before a Railway flip, that omits it.

findings.title: CLAUDE.md's 'All flags default OFF in code' is false — 22 ENABLE_* flags in app/ default to true, and the same paragraph contradicts itself two sentences later
findings.claim: The Feature Flags paragraph asserts 'All flags default OFF in code; flip in Railway during canary', but an AST scan of every os.getenv in app/ finds 22 ENABLE_*/DISABLE_* flags whose literal default is a truthy string.
findings.evidence: CLAUDE.md:328 contains both 'All flags default OFF in code; flip in Railway during canary.' and, ~40 words later, '`ENABLE_EXACT_PRICE_GATE` (default ON, IN PROD ...)'. AST enumeration of app/ (164 getenv/environ calls, 128 unique names) finds these default-ON flags: ENABLE_ADAPTER_QUERY_LADDER (price_service.py:6251), ENABLE_ADAPTER_SELECTION_PRIMARY (:6286), ENABLE_BUDGET_FRAGRANCE_FLOOR (:4303), ENABLE_EARLY_SPECS_STASH (structured_comparison_service.py:1926), ENABLE_EXACT_PRICE_GATE (price_service.py:4002), ENABLE_FAIRNESS_IGNORE_ESTIMATE (:4403), ENABLE_FIRECRAWL (firecrawl_service.py:134), ENABLE_FIRECRAWL_RAW_HTML (:50), ENABLE_HOSTILE_NUMERIC_GUARD (price_service.py:4275), ENABLE_JSONLD_FIRST (:11189), ENABLE_JSONLD_SHAPE_LADDER (:10024), ENABLE_MONEY_PARSER_V2 (:3300), ENABLE_NASSER_ADAPTER (:14840), ENABLE_OG_BRANCH_FIXES (:4130), ENABLE_ORGANIC_PDP_HARVEST (structured_comparison_service.py:1908), ENABLE_PAGE_SCRAPE (price_service.py:41), ENABLE_PARK_LISTING_URL_TIER1 (structured_comparison_service.py:1945), ENABLE_PLATFORM_VERDICT (platform_router.py:473), ENABLE_SALE_PRICE_FIRST (price_service.py:4023), ENABLE_SCRAPEDO (scrapedo_service.py:104), ENABLE_STRICT_CURRENCY_LABEL (price_service.py:677), ENABLE_WIDE_CANDIDATE (price_service.py:4159). 13 of the 22 are absent from CLAUDE.md entirely.
findings.failure_scenario: An operator doing incident triage reads the blanket rule, concludes 'no flag is on unless Railway sets it', and does not think to check ENABLE_SALE_PRICE_FIRST / ENABLE_STRICT_CURRENCY_LABEL / ENABLE_MONEY_PARSER_V2 when a price regression appears — three default-ON price-parsing behaviours that are invisible in the Railway variables list precisely because they are defaults. The same rule makes a rollback plan wrong: setting a default-ON flag to nothing (deleting the Railway var) restores it to ON, not OFF.
findings.fix_sketch: Replace the blanket sentence with 'default is per-flag; the default is written next to each flag below', and add the 13 undocumented default-ON flags. A cheap CI guard: a test that AST-scans app/ for ENABLE_*/DISABLE_* getenv defaults and asserts every name appears in CLAUDE.md — it would have caught all of this and keeps catching it.
findings.verify_evidence: INDEPENDENTLY RE-DERIVED with my own AST scan of app/ (written to scratchpad envscan.py): 128 unique os.getenv/os.environ.get names and exactly 22 ENABLE_*/DISABLE_* flags whose literal default is truthy — the same 22 names the finding lists, at the same file:line. Spot-checked the truthiness semantics at four sites so this is not a string-matching artifact: price_service.py:677 `os.getenv("ENABLE_STRICT_CURRENCY_LABEL", "true").strip().lower() not in ("false","0","no","off","")`, same shape at price_service.py:3300 (MONEY_PARSER_V2) and platform_router.py:473 (PLATFORM_VERDICT), and price_service.py:14840 `os.environ.get("ENABLE_NASSER_ADAPTER", "true").lower() != "false"` — all genuinely default-ON. CLAUDE.md:328 does contain both 'All flags default OFF in code; flip in Railway during canary.' and '`ENABLE_EXACT_PRICE_GATE` (default ON, IN PROD ...)' in the same paragraph. Re-counted the documentation gap myself: of the 22, exactly 13 have grep count 0 in CLAUDE.md (ADAPTER_QUERY_LADDER, ADAPTER_SELECTION_PRIMARY, BUDGET_FRAGRANCE_FLOOR, HOSTILE_NUMERIC_GUARD, JSONLD_SHAPE_LADDER, MONEY_PARSER_V2, NASSER_ADAPTER, OG_BRANCH_FIXES, ORGANIC_PDP_HARVEST, PARK_LISTING_URL_TIER1, SALE_PRICE_FIRST, STRICT_CURRENCY_LABEL, WIDE_CANDIDATE). The rollback consequence the finding names is real and is the sharpest part: deleting a Railway var for one of these restores ON, not OFF.

findings.title: 65 of the 128 environment variables app/ reads are undocumented in CLAUDE.md, including 26 feature flags and 3 with no safe default
findings.claim: An AST enumeration of every os.getenv / os.environ access in app/ yields 128 distinct names; 65 of them appear nowhere in CLAUDE.md, and three scoring knobs are read with `os.getenv(NAME)` and no default at all.
findings.evidence: AST scan of app/ (164 call sites). Undocumented flags: ENABLE_ADAPTER_QUERY_LADDER, ENABLE_ADAPTER_SELECTION_PRIMARY, ENABLE_ASYNC_REDIS_OFFLOAD, ENABLE_BRIGHTDATA_BUDGET_GATE, ENABLE_BUDGET_FRAGRANCE_FLOOR, ENABLE_CONTENT_SAFETY_TEST_SEEDS, ENABLE_FRAGRANCE_SIZE_RECONCILE_FIX, ENABLE_GENUINE_PRICE_PRIORITY, ENABLE_GPT_WINNER, ENABLE_HOSTILE_NUMERIC_GUARD, ENABLE_JSONLD_SHAPE_LADDER, ENABLE_MONEY_PARSER_V2, ENABLE_NASSER_ADAPTER, ENABLE_OG_BRANCH_FIXES, ENABLE_ORGANIC_PDP_HARVEST, ENABLE_PARK_LISTING_URL_TIER1, ENABLE_PRICE_TITLE_PERSIST, ENABLE_SALE_PRICE_FIRST, ENABLE_SERPER_FAIL_FAST, ENABLE_STRICT_CURRENCY_LABEL, ENABLE_VARIANT_DESCRIPTOR_AXES, ENABLE_VARIANT_LLM_HINT, ENABLE_VARIANT_MIN_PRICE_GUARD, ENABLE_WIDE_CANDIDATE, ENABLE_YOUTUBE_SOURCE, DISABLE_DIM_NORM_DAMPENING. Undocumented tuning knobs with real blast radius: FAN_OUT_BUDGET_SECONDS (structured_comparison_service.py:1169, default '12.0'), GENUINE_MIN_BUDGET_SECONDS (:1218, '6.0'), RENDER_WAVE_MAX_DOMAINS (:1306, '2'), GENUINE_PRICE_CACHE_TTL_SECONDS (price_service.py:147, 7d), NEGATIVE_PRICE_CACHE_TTL_SECONDS (:148, 30d), MAX_MONTHLY_COST (cache_service.py:712, '100'), FREE_TIER_DAILY_LIMIT (cache_service.py:665, '5'), ZYTE_TIMEOUT (zyte_service.py:53, '100'), SCRAPEDO_GEOCODE (scrapedo_service.py:59, 'bh'). No-default reads: WINNER_DIM_GAP_TOLERANCE (scoring_service.py:360), WINNER_PRICE_AUTHORITY_POINTS (:673), WINNER_VALUE_WEIGHT_SCALE (:704) — these return None when unset and each site must handle it.
findings.failure_scenario: FREE_TIER_DAILY_LIMIT (cache_service.py:665) defaults to 5 while CLAUDE.md:162 documents the free daily cap as 3. An operator reconciling a billing complaint against the documented '3/day' has no way to learn from CLAUDE.md that a fifth env var exists that sets 5, and no way to know which of the two numbers the running service uses. Multiply by 64 more names: every incident that turns on 'what is this box actually configured to do' starts by reading source, because the documented env surface covers half the real one.
findings.fix_sketch: Generate the env-var section instead of hand-writing it: a script that AST-scans app/ + scripts/ and emits name/default/file:line, checked into docs/ and diffed by a CI test. That also makes the phantom-flag class (a Railway var with zero code refs, e.g. the documented ENABLE_HYBRID_MODEL_ROUTING) detectable from the other direction.
findings.verify_evidence: ENUMERATION EXACT, BOTH CONCRETE HAZARDS REFUTED. My own AST scan reproduces the headline numbers precisely: 128 unique names in app/, 65 absent from CLAUDE.md, 26 of those undocumented names are ENABLE_*/DISABLE_* — and my undocumented-flag list is character-for-character the finding's list. The tuning-knob defaults check out too (FAN_OUT_BUDGET_SECONDS '12.0' at structured_comparison_service.py:1169, RENDER_WAVE_MAX_DOMAINS '2' at :1306, ZYTE_TIMEOUT '100', SCRAPEDO_GEOCODE 'bh'). BUT: (1) the marquee failure scenario is dead code. FREE_TIER_DAILY_LIMIT is read once at cache_service.py:665 and used only by check_rate_limit (:668-685); `grep -rn 'check_rate_limit|get_user_daily_usage' app/ scripts/ tests/` outside cache_service.py returns NOTHING, so the '5' can never contradict the documented 3/day (usage_service is the live enforcement, CLAUDE.md:162) and no operator can be misled by it in the way described. (2) The 'three scoring knobs with no default at all ... return None when unset and each site must handle it' claim is wrong on inspection: scoring_service.py:358-367, :671-679 and :702-710 each read the var and IMMEDIATELY do `if raw is None: return <module default>` (_DEFAULT_DIM_GAP_TOLERANCE=0.08, _DEFAULT_PRICE_AUTHORITY_POINTS, 1.0), plus a try/except on the float parse — they are as safe as a getenv default. What remains is a documentation-coverage count that heavily overlaps data-05, with no demonstrated cost: P3.

findings.title: cohort_priors loader catches two exception types where its sibling loaders catch everything, and its two auth call sites are unguarded
findings.claim: `CohortService._load_cohort_priors` catches only FileNotFoundError and json.JSONDecodeError and never checks that the parsed document is a dict, so a valid-JSON-but-wrong-shape store, a non-UTF-8 byte, or a permission error escapes into two auth endpoints that call `get_cohort_service()` with no try/except.
findings.evidence: app/services/cohort_service.py:72-84 — `with open(PRIORS_PATH, encoding='utf-8') as f: return json.load(f)` guarded by `except FileNotFoundError` (:77) and `except json.JSONDecodeError` (:82) only. No `isinstance(data, dict)` check, unlike every sibling loader in the same tree: spec_spine_service.py:182-184 rejects a non-dict store, source_router.py:498 rejects a non-list catalog, home_routes.py:632-633 rejects a non-dict curated file. The singleton at cohort_service.py:348-352 caches whatever the first call produced for process lifetime. Call sites app/api/auth_routes.py:972 (`POST /auth/demographics`) and :1030 (profile style card) call `get_cohort_service()` bare; the three other call sites (extraction_service.py:1767, structured_comparison_service.py:4071) DO wrap it in try/except, which is what makes the two unguarded ones stand out.
findings.failure_scenario: `scripts/build_cohorts.py` is re-run and emits a list (or the file is committed with a BOM/latin-1 byte from a Windows editor — CLAUDE.md already records the cp1252 trap as a recurring gotcha). `json.load` raises UnicodeDecodeError, which is a ValueError but NOT a json.JSONDecodeError, so it propagates: `POST /auth/demographics` returns 500 for every user submitting the onboarding cohort modal, and the profile style card 500s, for the whole process lifetime. If instead the file parses to a list, the failure is deferred to `self._cohorts.get('cohorts', {})` -> AttributeError at the same two endpoints.
findings.fix_sketch: Widen to `except Exception` and add `if not isinstance(data, dict): return {'cohorts': {}, 'fallback_aggregates': {}}` — matching spec_spine_service.load_store, which is the house pattern. Then wrap the two auth_routes call sites the way the other three call sites already are.
findings.verify_evidence: READ AND RE-DERIVED. app/services/cohort_service.py:72-84: `with open(PRIORS_PATH, encoding="utf-8") as f: return json.load(f)` with handlers for FileNotFoundError (:77) and json.JSONDecodeError (:82) only, and no isinstance check — so UnicodeDecodeError (a ValueError, NOT a JSONDecodeError), PermissionError and OSError all escape, and a valid-JSON list is returned as-is. The house-pattern contrast is real, all three cited siblings verified: spec_spine_service.py:177-184 catches (OSError, ValueError) AND rejects a non-dict; source_router.py:497-505 catches bare Exception and degrades to literals; home_routes.py:631-633 rejects a non-dict curated file. Call-site claim independently grepped: get_cohort_service has exactly 4 runtime call sites — auth_routes.py:972 (POST /auth/demographics) and :1030 (profile style card) are BARE, while extraction_service.py:1767-1769 and structured_comparison_service.py:4071-4072 are inside try/except. ENABLE_COHORT_PERSONALIZATION is ON in prod (CLAUDE.md:328) and data/cohort_priors.json is a 114KB committed file regenerated by scripts/build_cohorts.py, so the 'bad regeneration -> 500 on two auth endpoints' path is live-reachable. Severity held at P2, not raised: the committed store is well-formed today, so this is a hardening gap, not an active break.

findings.title: 16 of 30 forward migrations have no rollback file, while CLAUDE.md presents the rollback directory without qualification
findings.claim: CLAUDE.md:83 says 'Files in `migrations/*.sql`; rollbacks in `migrations/rollback/*.sql`' as though the mapping were total; in fact migrations/rollback/ contains 14 files covering only 023-035, and 001, 002, 010-022 and add_share_token.sql have none.
findings.evidence: Directory listing: migrations/ holds 001, 002, 010-035 and add_share_token.sql (30 .sql files); migrations/rollback/ holds 023_referral_lifetime_cap_ROLLBACK.sql, 024_pre_rollback_downgrade.sql, 024_top_tier_budget.sql, and 025-035 (14 files). Uncovered forward migrations include the ones with the widest blast radius: 010_enable_rls.sql (15 CREATE statements — RLS + policies across every user table), 012_product_data_tables.sql (17 CREATEs, the whole L2 cache schema), 017_widen_share_token.sql (a column TYPE change), 014_referral_system.sql (16 CREATEs).
findings.failure_scenario: A 010-era policy change has to be reverted under time pressure (the exact scenario the rollback directory exists for). The operator opens migrations/rollback/, finds nothing for 010, and has to reconstruct the pre-010 RLS posture by hand from a migration that only says ENABLE — the pre-state is not recorded anywhere in the repo. The 025 rollback shows the team knows how to do this properly (it pins the exact prior function body); the gap is that the doc claims coverage the directory does not have.
findings.fix_sketch: Either author the missing rollbacks (010/012/014/017 first — the destructive ones) or change CLAUDE.md:83 to 'rollbacks exist for 023 onward; 001-022 are forward-only, revert by hand'. A one-line test that asserts every migrations/NNN_*.sql has a matching rollback would then have to be scoped to NNN >= 023, which is itself the honest documentation.
findings.verify_evidence: COUNT RIGHT, DENOMINATOR AND PREMISE OFF. My own enumeration: migrations/ holds 29 .sql files (not 30) and migrations/rollback/ holds 14 covering migration numbers 023-035 (024 has two rollback files). Uncovered = 16, exactly as claimed, and it is the 001/002/010-022 + add_share_token.sql block. CREATE-statement counts re-counted and match: 010_enable_rls.sql 15, 012_product_data_tables.sql 17, 014_referral_system.sql 16, 017_widen_share_token.sql 2. Where the finding overreaches is the premise: CLAUDE.md:83 says 'Files in `migrations/*.sql`; rollbacks in `migrations/rollback/*.sql`' — that is a LOCATOR sentence, not an assertion of total coverage, so 'presents the rollback directory without qualification' is a reading, not a misstatement. And the uncovered set is entirely pre-023 DDL applied to prod long ago (010-022, per the 'Applied 010-032' ledger), i.e. the least likely to need a scripted revert. Real hygiene gap, worth the one-line doc fix, but P3.

findings.title: The running service writes a committed repo data file (variant_hint_learned.json) with a non-atomic truncating write whose failure permanently disables it
findings.claim: `_varhint_append_learned` does a read-modify-write of `data/variant_hint_learned.json` inside the process, with `open(path, 'w')` (truncate-then-write, no temp file, no lock), and the read leg lives in the same try block as the write — so one interrupted write leaves a truncated file that makes every subsequent append a silent no-op forever.
findings.evidence: app/services/price_service.py:8619-8636. Path is `os.path.join(os.path.dirname(__file__), '..', '..', 'data', 'variant_hint_learned.json')` (:8529) — inside the deployed source tree. :8624-8628 reads and json.loads the existing file, :8630 mutates the dict, :8631 opens the SAME path with mode 'w' and json.dumps into it. The whole body is one `try: ... except Exception: pass` (:8635-8636). No os.replace, no tempfile, no advisory lock.
findings.failure_scenario: Two effects. (1) A SIGTERM between truncate and flush (Railway sends one on every redeploy, and the warmer service is exactly the process that runs this path) leaves partial JSON on disk; on the next run `json.load` raises inside the try, the outer except swallows it, and NO write happens — the file is now permanently unreadable and the convergence store stops accumulating, with no log line saying so. (2) Even on the happy path the write lands on a Railway container filesystem and is destroyed by the next deploy, so the 'convergence' the docstring promises never converges unless a human happens to be running the warmer on a workstation and commits the diff.
findings.fix_sketch: Split the read from the write (so a corrupt file resets to `{}` and self-heals), and make the write atomic: dump to `path + '.tmp'` then `os.replace`. Then decide the storage question honestly — if this is meant to survive, it belongs in the Redis verdict cache that already exists two functions up (:8600-8617) or in Postgres, not in a file inside the deployment artifact.
findings.verify_evidence: CODE DEFECT CONFIRMED, IMPACT MUCH SMALLER. app/services/price_service.py:8618-8636 read exactly as described: one try block that json.loads the existing file at :8625-8628, mutates the dict at :8630, then reopens the SAME path with mode 'w' at :8631 (truncate-in-place, no tempfile, no os.replace, no lock), with `except Exception: pass` at :8635-8636 — so a corrupt file makes the read raise BEFORE the write and the append becomes a permanent silent no-op. Path at :8528-8530 is inside the deployed tree (app/services/../../data/variant_hint_learned.json), so the Railway-ephemerality point holds too. BUT the blast radius the finding assigns ('the convergence store stops accumulating') is near-zero: I grepped for every reference to _VARHINT_LEARNED_PATH / 'variant_hint_learned' across app/, scripts/ and tests/ — the file is WRITE-ONLY, nothing in the codebase ever reads it back, so corruption has no runtime effect at all. The single writer (price_service.py:8672) sits behind ENABLE_VARIANT_LLM_HINT (default OFF, :8541) which hard-requires ENABLE_VARIANT_DESCRIPTOR_AXES, on the off-clock warmer path. Correct as a code-quality fix (split the read from the write, os.replace), not as a P2.

findings.title: The cold-start cron runbook baked into main.py points at a Railway host no other reference in the repo uses
findings.claim: The copy-pasteable warm-ping command in app/main.py names `smartcompare-backend-production.up.railway.app`, while all 10 other production-URL references in the tree (CLAUDE.md, scripts/eval_runner.py:66, the live-suite) name `web-production-58776.up.railway.app`.
findings.evidence: app/main.py:258-262: '# Set up a Railway cron service that pings GET /health every 5 minutes: / #   Command:  curl -sf https://smartcompare-backend-production.up.railway.app/health'. `grep -o 'https://[a-z0-9-]*\.up\.railway\.app'` over CLAUDE.md, scripts/ and app/ returns web-production-58776 x10 and smartcompare-backend-production x1 (this comment); the only other occurrences of the second host are in docs/plans/2026-02-* archives.
findings.failure_scenario: An operator sets up the anti-cold-start cron from this comment. `curl -sf` is silent-on-failure by design, so the cron reports success forever while pinging a host that is not the deployed service — the ~10-20s cold-start penalty the comment exists to remove stays in place on every idle-then-first request, and nothing surfaces the mistake.
findings.fix_sketch: Replace the host with web-production-58776, or better, drop the hostname and write `curl -sf "$RAILWAY_PUBLIC_DOMAIN/health"` so the comment cannot go stale again.
findings.verify_evidence: Read app/main.py:258-262 directly: '# Set up a Railway cron service that pings GET /health every 5 minutes:' / '#   Command:  curl -sf https://smartcompare-backend-production.up.railway.app/health'. Ran my own host census over app/, scripts/, tests/ and CLAUDE.md — `grep -roh 'https://[a-z0-9-]*\.up\.railway\.app'` gives web-production-58776 x30 and smartcompare-backend-production x1 (this comment), an even wider margin than the 10-vs-1 claimed. `curl -sf` is indeed silent on failure, so a cron built from this comment reports success forever while warming nothing. Stale copy-pasteable runbook line: P3 is right.

findings.title: Four response-dump JSON artifacts are committed at the repo root with zero code references
findings.claim: full_response.json, session23_test_response.json, UsersSynAckITPCDocumentsAIsmartcomparetmp_result.json and UsersSynAckITPCDocumentsAIsmartcomparetmp_luxury_test.json (~53KB) sit in the repo root, are referenced by nothing in app/, scripts/, tests/ or CLAUDE.md, and slip past the `response_*.json` .gitignore rule.
findings.evidence: Root listing shows the four files (16555, 10471, 10807, 15381 bytes). `grep -rl` for each name across app/ scripts/ tests/ CLAUDE.md returns nothing. .gitignore:32 is `response_*.json`, which matches none of the four (two are prefixed with a mangled absolute Windows path, one is `full_response.json`, one `session23_...`). Scanned for secrets/PII (email, user_id, token, uuid patterns): none present, so this is bloat rather than exposure.
findings.failure_scenario: Every clone and every Railway build ships 53KB of a developer's 2026-era debugging output; the two path-mangled names in particular read as accidental redirect targets from a Windows shell, which is exactly the kind of file that gets 'fixed' by someone who assumes it is load-bearing. Cost is small but exactly measurable, and the .gitignore rule that was meant to prevent this class does not cover it.
findings.fix_sketch: Delete the four files and broaden .gitignore to `*_response.json`, `full_response.json`, `Users*tmp_*.json`.
findings.verify_evidence: All four files exist at the repo root and are GIT-TRACKED (`git ls-files` lists full_response.json, session23_test_response.json, UsersSynAckITPCDocumentsAIsmartcomparetmp_result.json, UsersSynAckITPCDocumentsAIsmartcomparetmp_luxury_test.json); sizes 16555/10471/10812/15391 = 53,229 bytes. Absence claim checked myself two ways: `grep -rl` for each basename across the whole tree returns nothing, and the three root parse_*.py scripts that might have consumed them all take the path from sys.argv (parse_result.py:3 defaults to an ABSOLUTE C:\Users\...\smartcompare\tmp_result.json outside this repo, parse_luxury.py:3 uses sys.argv[1], parse_live.py:2 reads stdin). .gitignore:32 is `response_*.json`, which matches none of the four. I also ran the finding's secrets/PII sweep independently (emails, user_id, token, bearer, JWT prefix): zero hits, so bloat, not exposure. P3 confirmed.

findings.title: CLAUDE.md pins the catalog registry at '274 liveness-gated rows'; the committed store now yields 275
findings.claim: The ENABLE_BH_GCC_CATALOG_SOURCES entry says the flag 'loads the 274 liveness-gated BH/GCC catalog rows from data/bh_gcc_sources.json'; the file holds 275 status="live" rows and the loader admits all 275.
findings.evidence: data/bh_gcc_sources.json status histogram: live 275, dead 61, provider-test-candidate 18, render-only 14 (368 total). Executed with ENABLE_BH_GCC_CATALOG_SOURCES=true: `len(source_router._load_catalog_rows()) == 275`, `len(_LITERAL_ROWS) == 44`, `len(SOURCE_REGISTRY) == 319`. CLAUDE.md:328 says 274.
findings.failure_scenario: Low cost on its own, but it is the number an operator uses to confirm the flag took effect after a deploy ('registry should be literals+274'). Off-by-one against a hand-maintained count means the check either fails spuriously or is quietly ignored, and once ignored it stops detecting a genuine registry regression.
findings.fix_sketch: Stop hand-maintaining the count in prose. `scripts/build_source_registry_data.py --stats` already prints the by-status histogram; either reference that command or add the live-row count to a test that also updates nothing (assert `len(_load_catalog_rows()) == len([r for r in json rows if r['status']=='live'])`, which is drift-proof).
findings.verify_evidence: Reproduced both numbers. data/bh_gcc_sources.json status histogram computed here: live 275, dead 61, provider-test-candidate 18, render-only 14 (368 total). With ENABLE_BH_GCC_CATALOG_SOURCES=true, `len(source_router._load_catalog_rows()) == 275` and `len(SOURCE_REGISTRY) == 319` (so 44 literals). CLAUDE.md:328 says the flag 'loads the 274 liveness-gated BH/GCC catalog rows'. Off by one, in the exact number an operator would use as a post-deploy confirmation. P3.

findings.title: spec_spine_service.lookup returns the memoised store's inner dict by reference, so a caller mutation poisons the process-wide store
findings.claim: `lookup()` returns `load_store().get(key)` — the live object inside the `_STORE_CACHE` memo — so any caller that mutates the returned entry changes what every subsequent lookup in the process sees, until the file's mtime changes.
findings.evidence: app/services/spec_spine_service.py:313-314 (`entry = load_store().get(key)` / `return entry if isinstance(entry, dict) else None`). `load_store` (:158-186) caches the parsed document in `_STORE_CACHE` keyed on (path, mtime_ns, size) and returns the cached object itself at :175. The in-tree consumer `spine_specs_for` is safe because `_entry_specs` (:268-291) builds a fresh dict, but `lookup` is exported in `__all__` (:69-80) and documented at :304-310 as the entry point 'so the seeder and tests can read the store directly'.
findings.failure_scenario: `scripts/seed_spec_spine.py` (or a future refill path) calls `lookup()`, finds a thin row, and updates `entry['specs']['sillage'] = ...` in place before persisting. Because the store is memoised by mtime and the seeder writes with `--out` to a different path, the in-memory store now serves an unpersisted value for the rest of the process — the classic 'works in the seed run, gone after restart' bug, and the reverse (an in-place delete) silently removes a spine hit that is still on disk. Currently latent: data/spec_spine.json ships `{}`, so there is nothing to mutate yet.
findings.fix_sketch: Return `copy.deepcopy(entry)` from `lookup`, or freeze the store on load. One line, and it closes the hole before the store is seeded.
findings.verify_evidence: Core mechanism true: app/services/spec_spine_service.py:312-313 is `entry = load_store().get(key)` / `return entry if isinstance(entry, dict) else None`, and load_store (:158-186) returns the memoised object itself from _STORE_CACHE at :174-175 — so lookup hands out a live reference into the process-wide store. Docstring at :302-304 does invite exactly the risky use ('so the seeder and tests can read the store directly'). Two supporting claims are WRONG and I am recording them: (a) there is NO `__all__` in spec_spine_service.py at all (grepped the whole file) — lines 69-80 are the module docstring and imports, so 'exported in __all__ (:69-80)' is fabricated; (b) scripts/seed_spec_spine.py:71-75 imports only SPINE_CATEGORY, SPINE_FIELDS and spine_key — it never calls lookup, so the named scenario has no author today. Latency of the bug also confirmed: data/spec_spine.json is literally `{}` (4 bytes) and the only in-tree caller is spine_specs_for:346, which copies via _entry_specs. Correct as a P3 one-line hardening.

findings.title: CLAUDE.md describes the seeded search-descriptor store as 'robots-allowed rows only'; 2 of the 95 persisted rows carry robots_allowed=false
findings.claim: The M7 entry says data/search_descriptors.json was 'populated with 95 resolved fragrance hosts (47 usable {q} templates; robots-allowed rows only)', but two of the 95 rows record robots_allowed=false and are folded onto their registry rows all the same.
findings.evidence: data/search_descriptors.json hosts: 95 entries; `robots_allowed` is false for bdutyfree.com and ounass.ae, both `kind: 'none'`, `url_template: ''`, `discovered_via: 'platform_probe'`. Both are folded onto live registry rows in data/bh_gcc_sources.json (95 rows carry a `search` block, matching the store exactly). They are functionally inert today because `SearchDescriptor.usable` (app/services/search_descriptor_service.py:135-144) requires kind in (platform_api, onsite_html) AND robots_allowed AND a '{q}' template — all three fail here.
findings.failure_scenario: The doc sentence teaches a reader that robots enforcement happens at RESOLVE time and the store is pre-filtered. It does not: the store persists disallowed answers on purpose (recording a resolved 'no' so it is never re-probed) and enforcement lives in the `usable` property. A future contributor who trusts the doc could add a template to one of those rows, or write a consumer that reads `url_template` without going through `usable`, and the robots gate silently disappears — the exact house-rule-7 class the module's own docstring (:47-52) says is enforced in code, not comments.
findings.fix_sketch: Reword to '95 resolved hosts, 47 usable {q} templates; robots-disallowed hosts are persisted as resolved dead ends and gated by SearchDescriptor.usable'. Costs one sentence and prevents a real regression.
findings.verify_evidence: Every sub-claim checked against the files. CLAUDE.md:334 does read 'populated with 95 resolved fragrance hosts (47 usable `{q}` templates; robots-allowed rows only)'. data/search_descriptors.json: 95 hosts, 47 with a {q} template (both counts computed here), and robots_allowed is False for exactly two — bdutyfree.com and ounass.ae, each `kind: 'none'`, `url_template: ''`, `discovered_via: 'platform_probe'`. Both ARE folded onto live registry rows in data/bh_gcc_sources.json (I printed the rows: status 'live', search block byte-identical to the store), and 95 registry rows carry a search block, matching the store exactly. The code gate is correct as the finding says: SearchDescriptor.usable (search_descriptor_service.py:131-143) requires kind in (platform_api, onsite_html) AND robots_allowed AND '{q}', so both rows are inert today. Documentation wording defect only: P3.

findings.title: The fixture that stops the test suite writing a committed data file is opt-in, not autouse
findings.claim: `no_learned_write` — which monkeypatches out the `data/variant_hint_learned.json` write so 'the suite never touches the committed data file' — is a plain fixture that each test must request, and 7 of the 20 tests in the module do not.
findings.evidence: tests/test_variant_llm_hint_b3b.py:63-67 defines the fixture with a docstring stating its purpose; 14 of 20 test signatures name it. The 7 that do not (test_cache_hit_distinct_no_llm_call, test_cache_hit_same_no_llm_call, test_sync_veto_reads_verdict_cache, test_off_by_default, test_requires_axes, test_requires_exact_gate, test_on_when_all_set) are all cache-hit or flag-off cases that never reach `_varhint_append_learned`, so the suite is safe TODAY. tests/conftest.py has 8 autouse fixtures but none of them covers this path.
findings.failure_scenario: Someone adds a 21st test that exercises the high-confidence LLM branch — the branch the module exists to test — and forgets the fixture. `_varhint_append_learned` (app/services/price_service.py:8619) then rewrites the committed data/variant_hint_learned.json during `pytest tests/`, and the developer's next `git status` shows a data-file diff produced by running the test suite. Because the writer swallows all exceptions, there is no signal at test time that it happened.
findings.fix_sketch: Promote it to an autouse fixture in tests/conftest.py (patch `price_service._varhint_append_learned` to a no-op for the whole suite) and let the one test that actually wants to assert the write opt back in with monkeypatch. That is the same posture tests/_env_safety.py already takes for credentials.
findings.verify_evidence: Verified in the file. tests/test_variant_llm_hint_b3b.py:63-67 defines `no_learned_write` as a plain (non-autouse) fixture whose docstring is 'Suppress the data/variant_hint_learned.json write so the suite never touches the committed data file.' `pytest --collect-only -q` on the module collects 20 tests; 13 test signatures request the fixture (the finding's '14 of 20' counted the `def` line) and the 7 that do not are exactly the ones listed (test_cache_hit_distinct_no_llm_call, test_cache_hit_same_no_llm_call, test_sync_veto_reads_verdict_cache, test_off_by_default, test_requires_axes, test_requires_exact_gate, test_on_when_all_set) — all cache-hit or flag-gate cases that never reach _varhint_append_learned, so the suite is safe today as claimed. tests/conftest.py has 7 autouse fixtures (not 8: two of the nine 'autouse' lines are comments) — _scoped_rate_limiter_bypass, _reset_pain_workflow_cache, _reset_verdict_exemplar_cache, _reset_variant_descriptor_memo, _reset_serper_budget_gate_memo, _ensure_event_loop_present, _reset_rate_limiter — and none patches the learned-file write. Opt-in-fixture-as-safety-net: P3.
